verdict_reason: The delimiter swap itself is correct and consistent with bridge/fulfilment-id.js, but it introduces a third unenforced copy of INDEX_DELIMITER in model/ and leaves the file's 'path' vocabulary half-renamed.

todos.issue: INDEX_DELIMITER is now a private copy that must silently agree with bridge/fulfilment-id.js#INDEX_DELIMITER, and the same copy-plus-comment appears in two other model files (obligations/state-queries.js:12, obligations/helpers/projection/internals/filter-and-project.js:5); nothing enforces the agreement, so a future delimiter change to the bridge constant leaves these three splitting on the wrong character and silently mis-parsing fulfilment indexes rather than failing
todos.fix: Hoist one model-local constant (e.g. src/server/app/model/obligations/index-delimiter.js) imported by all three model files - permitted by the dep-cruiser model-import-boundary rule, which only bans model -> bridge - and add a test importing both it and bridge's INDEX_DELIMITER asserting they are equal (test files are excluded from dep-cruiser)

todos.issue: The rename stopped at the constant: PATH_DELIMITER became INDEX_DELIMITER but joinPath/splitPath (lines 6-7) and instancePathPrefixesFromRecord still speak the old 'path' vocabulary for values that are now fulfilment indexes (line0.unit1), leaving the file half-migrated against AC 3 (consistent 'fulfilment index' naming)
todos.fix: Rename the file-local helpers to joinIndex/splitIndex (and instancePathPrefixesFromRecord -> indexPrefixesFromRecord) so the vocabulary matches the constant and the callers' fulfilmentIndex naming
